title: Slot allocation efficiency curvature benchmark - annotated notes
content:
Executive summary:

This note captures an ad-hoc benchmark we ran to understand how slot allocation granularity ("slots" = opportunistic execution windows on GPUs) interacts with latency tail, throughput efficiency, and per-token unit cost for bursty conversational workloads. The aim is to produce a short set of tradeoff visuals in text form for inclusion in the optimize playbook and an internal one-pager for product.

Key takeaways (high level):
- Fine-grained slots (ShortSlot=50ms scheduling quanta) reduce mean cold-start latency for very short requests but increase wasted GPU time and unit cost by ~6–12% under moderate sustained load due to fill inefficiency.
- Coarse-grained slots (LongSlot=500ms) improve batching efficiency and cost per token by up to 18% for sessionized workloads with multi-turn context, but can increase p99 latency for single-turn, low-QPS bursts.
- A mid-point curvature policy (adaptive slot length that increases with detected session length and KV cache hit rate) achieves ~10% cost savings vs ShortSlot and keeps p99 within 1.1x of ShortSlot across our test vectors.

Bench objective and motivation:
- Problem: standard fixed-slot allocation policies are a blunt instrument — they either favor low-latency single-turn requests or batched throughput for sticky sessions.
- Hypothesis: an adaptive slot policy guided by session shape and KV cache hit rate will give a Pareto improvement in cost vs latency for typical customer mixes.

Experiment setup:
- Cluster: 8 x A100-80GB GPU nodes, 64 vCPU, 512GB RAM each, running serving-runtime v2.7.1-rc (kernel scheduling changes in PR).
- Model: redwood-7b-chat (fp16), sequence length cap 2048, KV cache enabled.
- Workloads: three synthetic arrival profiles derived from production traces (anonymized):
  * ShortBurst: median request 35 tokens, session length 1, QPS spikes to 400 for 10s every 2 minutes.
  * SessionSticky: median request 120 tokens, session length 6 turns, steady QPS 80.
  * MixedCurve: 60% ShortBurst, 30% SessionSticky, 10% long-chat 500 token sessions.
- Policies tested:
  * ShortSlot (50ms quantum, immediate preemptible scheduling)
  * LongSlot (500ms quantum, coalescing enabled)
  * AdaptiveCurvature (starts at 100ms, doubles after each turn if session detected until 400ms cap, KV-hit lowers growth rate)
- Metrics collected: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (endpoint-to-first-token), tail CPU/GPU utilization, tokens/sec, cost estimate modeled from per-GPU minute billing + amortized infra.

Raw (text) charts and tables (annotated):

1) Latency percentiles (ms) by policy, MixedCurve workload
+----------------+---------+---------+---------+---------+
| Policy         | p50     | p90     | p95     | p99     |
+----------------+---------+---------+---------+---------+
| ShortSlot      | 34      | 128     | 210     | 540     |
| LongSlot       | 40      | 110     | 175     | 760     |
| AdaptiveCurv   | 36      | 115     | 182     | 590     |
+----------------+---------+---------+---------+---------+
Notes: ShortSlot lowers p99 vs LongSlot for sub-100ms flows; LongSlot p50 is slightly higher due to coalescing delay. Adaptive keeps p99 close to ShortSlot while improving p95.

2) Cost per 1M tokens (USD estimate) by policy, MixedCurve workload
+----------------+-----------------+
| Policy         | cost_per_1M_tok |
+----------------+-----------------+
| ShortSlot      | $1180           |
| LongSlot       | $980            |
| AdaptiveCurv   | $1065           |
+----------------+-----------------+
Note: cost modeled includes GPU-minutes, infra overhead, and token emission compute. ShortSlot has higher cost because of lower concealment of idle slots.

3) GPU utilization over test window (aggregate, %), SessionSticky workload
- ShortSlot: mean GPU util 62%, std 14%
- LongSlot: mean GPU util 85%, std 6%
- AdaptiveCurv: mean GPU util 78%, std 9%
Interpretation: LongSlot achieves higher steady-state utilization which maps to lower per-token charge; variance is important for tail SLOs.

4) KV cache hit sensitivity (MixedCurve): p99 vs KV hit ratio
ASCII sparkline: p99_latency(ms) as KV_hit rises from 0% -> 80%
- ShortSlot: 680 -> 510 (drop ~25%)
- LongSlot: 820 -> 630 (drop ~23%)
- AdaptiveCurv: 640 -> 480 (drop ~25%)
Observation: all policies benefit from KV caching; AdaptiveCurv preserves p99 benefits of caching while not regressing cost.

Micro-insights and puzzlers (notes for follow-up):
- Micro-waste: we observed that ShortSlot has many sub-quantum interruptions where dispatch overhead (RPC + scheduler context) consumes ~6–9% of a slot; need to quantify whether batching at the client side or request coalescer is cheaper than increasing slot quantum.
- Preemption penalty: LongSlot occasionally suffers preemption cascades when a large session enters a slot that was coalesced; this leads to instant p99 spikes. Can mitigate with per-session reservation tokens.
- Cold-start shape: Single-turn cold-starts benefit more from smaller slots, but for multi-turn sticky sessions the amortization dominates.

Suggested visuals to produce from this sketch (for product one-pager):
- MixedCurve: 2x mini charts: cost-per-1M tokens vs p99 latency for each policy (scatter with policy labels).
- Heatmap: slot quantum (x-axis) vs average KV hit (y-axis) -> cost delta (cells).
- Timeline: example burst event showing spike QPS and the different response shapes for the 3 policies.

Action items and TODOs: (owner in parens)
- Re-run MixedCurve with redwood-70b-chat quantized variant to check whether larger models amplify cost deltas (Marcus).
- Add a client-side coalescer test: set service to ShortSlot but add a 10ms client buffer to batch short requests and measure tradeoffs (Aisha).
- Instrument scheduler: add per-slot wasted-ms metric and expose in console as 'slot_efficiency' (Luis, infra ticket created ENGOBS-789).
- Product: draft two lines for the optimize playbook describing AdaptiveCurvature policy and recommended default for Hosted API (product review needed).

Open questions for review:
- For Dedicated customers with predictable reserved capacity, does coalescing policy need to be different? (Do they prefer LongSlot always?)
- What's an acceptable p99 delta for core PLG use-cases before we auto-escalate to smaller slots? 1.2x? 1.1x?

Appendix: experiment notes and reproducibility (quick)
- Configs: serving-runtime flags used: --slot-quantum-ms, --coalesce-window-ms, --preemptive-reserve=true/false, --kv-hit-growth-threshold=0.3 (experimental).
- Trace ids: anonymized runs stored in s3://redwood-experiments/slots/2027-09-14/ (internal only).
- Command used (sketch): bench/run_burst_sweep.sh --profile MixedCurve --slots=adaptive --nodes=8 --duration=30m --collect=latency,util,tokens

Comments (live):
- Luis: "We should try per-tenant adaptive caps before cluster-level, reduces cross-tenant tail coupling"
- Aisha: "Client-side buffering looks promising; need to ensure it doesn't break function/tool calling streaming semantics."

Bottom line (one line for exec): An adaptive slot curvature policy offers a strong middle ground — it captures most of the cost benefits of coalescing while preserving low tail latency for bursty single-turn traffic. Next step: a short public-friendly vignette + one internal console metric to demonstrate slot efficiency.
